posts.heading: September 17, 2026
posts.text:
Tufted Titmice held the feeder before the sun cleared the horizon, with the first confident sighting recorded at 07:02 and visits continuing through the morning. Carolina Chickadees and Tufted Titmice dominated the visual traffic, while Carolina Wrens and Northern Cardinals provided the primary vocal presence from early in the hour.

A Gray Catbird called thirteen times during the 09:00 hour, standing out among the background chorus of wrens and chickadees. House Finches arrived in small numbers, with ten confirmed visits, alongside occasional appearances by White-breasted Nuthatches and Mourning Doves.

The morning has built steadily from the pre-dawn arrivals to a diverse mix of species by late morning. Northern Cardinals were heard ten times in the past hour, adding to their total of twenty-four detections.

posts.heading: September 16, 2026
posts.text:
The station logged its busiest day of the week with 210 visits and 23 species, well above the previous seven-day average of 135 visits and 14 species. Tufted Titmice dominated the visual traffic with 104 confident sightings, while Carolina Wrens and Blue Jays provided the most frequent vocal presence. This surge in activity follows the installation of a new seed feeder on September 13, which replaced a unit that had previously caused detection issues.

Regulars such as the Carolina Chickadee, Northern Cardinal, and Mourning Dove held their usual presence throughout the day. A few occasional visitors, including a Northern Flicker and Eastern Phoebe, added to the total count during the afternoon.

The day ended with a Ruby-throated Hummingbird heard in the 20:00 hour and the last Tufted Titmouse visit at 19:19.

posts.heading: September 15, 2026
posts.text:
The station recorded 268 visits and 20 species, a sharp increase from the 96.7 visit average of the previous seven days. Tufted Titmice and Carolina Chickadees maintained their presence as regulars, while Mourning Doves and House Finches contributed to the visual count. The high activity level aligns with the installation of the new seed feeder and treat bowls earlier in the week, which have supported the station's recent rise in numbers.

A Black-capped Chickadee provided the station’s first confident visual record of the species, while a Common Gallinule was heard for the first time here. Neither species appears on the regional list for this time of year. Northern Cardinals and Blue Jays were active throughout the day, with the Cardinals producing a notable burst of vocalizations in the final hour.

The audio source change to the new microphone on September 13 did not result in any species being heard for the first time. The usual residents, including Carolina Wrens and Northern Mockingbirds, continued to be detected. The day concluded with a Carolina Chickadee as the last visual contact.

posts.heading: September 14, 2026
posts.text: Yesterday registered 232 feeder visits and 16 species, a sharp increase from the recent weekly average of 63.6 visits and 10.0 species. The station’s activity ramped up following the installation of a new seed feeder on the morning of September 13, which replaced a unit that had been causing detection issues. This hardware change aligns with the steady rise in visual traffic observed over the last two days, culminating in yesterday’s high volume of Tufted Titmouse and Carolina Chickadee interactions.
